source_text: Omnis adeps Domini est; non comedetis. Pinguedo gloriae Deo. Cor pinguem misericordiae. Amen.
thought_title: All fat belongs to the Lord
orientation: Origen is concluding his spiritual reading of the sacrifice of praise, applying the Levitical rule about fat to the soul's richest devotion.
pass_a_gloss: All fat is the Lord's; you shall not eat it. The richness of glory belongs to God. A heart rich in mercy. Amen.

choices.why: The Levitical term for the fatty portions reserved for God; kept literal to preserve the ritual sense.
Renders the abstract noun as a quality of glory, matching the spiritual application Origen makes.
Adjectival form applied to the heart, conveying moral fullness rather than physical fat.
Preserves the second-person plural prohibition of the Levitical command.

pass_b_english: All the fat belongs to the Lord; you shall not eat it (Leviticus 3:16). The richness of glory belongs to God. A heart rich in mercy. Amen.
